title: When does history restore what a snapshot loses?
summary: A short history makes some coarse views of Rule 110 much easier to predict. Changing the observation changes the result—and the proposed Class IV shortcut fails.
takeaway: What looks unpredictable in a snapshot can become predictable when we restore part of its path.

title: A zero commutator does not imply a linear rule
summary: Rules 4 and 200 are nonlinear, yet their commutators vanish. The earlier theorem needs a one-way implication, and the Concepts explanation has been corrected.
takeaway: A useful test can have exceptions. Preserving the counterexample is part of improving the explanation.

title: Are we predicting the background, or the moving structures?
summary: The original plan for separating background and disturbance errors, now linked to its completed frozen-protocol experiment.
takeaway: The regional test is complete; its results and remaining structural questions have their own note.

title: History helps around disturbances, too
summary: A frozen regional test finds that history improves prediction around ether departures as well as background. Most remaining errors still lie near departures.
takeaway: A path restores useful predictive context around disturbances, but a local detector does not tell us whether the predictor understands gliders.

promotion.idea: A path helps at disturbances, too

title: History and possibility: the wider research program
summary: How inherited structure enables further activity, when it becomes difficult to revise, and how to study capabilities alongside prediction.
takeaway: History matters through what it makes possible, including the ability to change the operations available next.

title: Operation order changes outcomes and how to reach them
summary: Exact enumeration separates prepared-state differences, reachable outcomes, and action responses. Equal numbers can hide different options; equal sets can hide different ways to act.
takeaway: Possibility needs an action vocabulary and a time budget. Count the options, identify them, and check how they are reached.

promotion.idea: The same options can require different actions

title: When does a useful shortcut become a constraint?
summary: A proposed comparison of reusable constructions that can be reopened versus constructions that become fixed, with equal resources and explicit revision costs.
takeaway: Inherited efficiency and the capacity to revise it need to be measured together. This experiment is proposed, not run.
